failure_summary.description: Search or filter results were not saved correctly: calls were omitted from caching or save statements referenced unassigned variables.
Follow-up constraints triggered fresh searches or repeated unaffected itinerary domains instead of reusing cached results.
State abbreviations for attraction searches were passed as city values rather than state values.
Flight searches used departure-time strings rejected by the tool.
The agent failed to derive checkout from an explicit stay length and also supplied an unstated guest count.

patch.reasoning: Cache handling, result saving, field mapping, and accepted time formats are already addressed explicitly in the skill, so restating them would duplicate existing guidance. Add the missing rule for deriving checkout when both a check-in date and an explicit number of nights are provided; vague timing and unstated occupancy must remain uninferred.

edits.content: - If the user provides a hotel check-in date and an explicit stay length in nights but no checkout date, derive checkout by calling `adjust_date` with the check-in date and the stated number of nights, then use its result. Do not derive dates from vague timing such as “weekend,” or infer unspecified guest or room counts.
